title: External current suppression and surface-temperature response of a commercial cylindrical cell under sequential source-voltage abuse
content: This exploratory analysis examines the external current and surface-temperature histories of one commercial cylindrical cell using 3985 successive observations at 1 s intervals. Programmed 5 and 10 V exposures were assigned from the current trace, with a transition at 29.28 min. Mean current magnitude decreased from 0.1243 to 0.0400 A; adjacent-window comparisons retained a 63.85–65.71% reduction for window lengths of 30–300 s. Setpoint-based energy estimates remained lower in the second stage when exposure durations were matched: 0.659 versus 1.023 kJ over 1645 s. The 64.9 °C surface maximum preceded the assigned transition by 7.92 min, establishing that the higher-setting interval inherited an already declining thermal trajectory. The second-stage mean smoothed temperature rate remained negative for 31–121 s windows, although local slope signs depended on the observation window. These analyses separate a persistent electrical contrast from duration and processing effects, while showing why it cannot establish a causal voltage effect or thermal safety. Cell chemistry, source operating state and the terminal-voltage waveform remain unverified or unavailable. The analysis identifies which features of this individual record persist across changes in window length, integration duration and smoothing.
